title: Yunus in the darkness
summary: Prophet Yunus left his people in anger and ended up swallowed by a great fish. In layers of darkness he called out to Allah, declaring His oneness, glorifying Him and admitting his own mistake. Allah answered him, rescued him from his distress, and said that He rescues the believers in the same way.
lesson: No darkness is too deep for a sincere call to Allah, and admitting our own fault opens the way out.
bridge: When the user feels trapped, has made a mistake, or feels there is no way out.
do_not_add: Do not state how long he was inside the fish, the species or size of the fish, or other details from Isra'iliyyat. Stay with what the Qur'an says.

title: Musa at the well of Madyan
summary: Musa fled Egypt alone, with nothing. At the wells of Madyan he saw two women waiting with their flock, and he watered it for them. Then he sat in the shade and told Allah that he was in need of whatever good He sent down to him. Soon one of the women came back with her father's invitation. Musa found safety, then work for several years, and then marriage.
lesson: Do what you can, help others along the way, and ask Allah plainly for what you need. Provision can come from where you least expect it.
bridge: When the user has lost a job, is searching for work, or feels alone in a new place.
do_not_add: The Qur'an does not name the women's father. Do not state as fact that he was Prophet Shu'ayb.

title: Fatimah asks for a servant
summary: Fatimah's hands were worn from grinding grain, and she and Ali asked the Prophet ﷺ for a servant. He came to them at night and taught them to say Allahu Akbar 34 times, SubhanAllah 33 times and Alhamdulillah 33 times before sleeping, telling them this was better for them than a servant.
lesson: When resources are tight, remembrance of Allah gives a strength that money cannot.
bridge: When the user is exhausted by work or money pressure.
do_not_add: Do not add details about their household or poverty beyond the hadith.

title: The three men in the cave
summary: Three travellers sheltered in a cave, and a rock rolled down and sealed it. Each man called on Allah by a good deed he had done sincerely: one by his care for his elderly parents, one by stopping himself from a sin, and one by honestly keeping a worker's unpaid wages, growing them, and giving the worker all of it when he returned. After each prayer the rock moved a little, until they walked out.
lesson: Sincere good deeds, especially honesty with others' money, are a way out in hardship.
bridge: When the user feels stuck, or is worried about honesty and money at work.
do_not_add: Do not add names, places or extra dialogue.

title: Ayyub's patience
summary: Prophet Ayyub was afflicted with harm. He called on his Lord gently, saying that harm had touched him and that Allah is the Most Merciful of the merciful. Allah removed his affliction, told him to strike the ground with his foot to bring out cool water to wash and drink, and restored his family and more. The Qur'an calls him patient and an excellent servant.
lesson: Patience is not silence. Ayyub told Allah of his pain, and was praised as patient.
bridge: When the user is ill or in long-term pain.
do_not_add: Do not mention the number of years, worms, or stories about his wife; these are not authentic.

title: Ya'qub's beautiful patience
summary: When his sons told him Yusuf was lost, Ya'qub chose 'beautiful patience'. Years later, losing another son, he grieved so deeply that his eyes turned white with sorrow. Yet he said he complained of his grief only to Allah, and told his sons to go and search and never to despair of Allah's mercy.
lesson: Grief and tears are allowed. Bring the grief to Allah, and do not give up hope.
bridge: When the user is grieving or waiting a long time for something to change.
do_not_add: Stay with the Qur'anic account; do not add years or Isra'iliyyat details.

title: The Prophet's tears for his son
summary: When the Prophet's infant son Ibrahim was dying, tears flowed from his eyes. When asked about it, he said it is mercy, and that the eyes shed tears and the heart grieves, but we say only what pleases our Lord.
lesson: Crying is not weak faith. The Prophet ﷺ grieved, and stayed content with Allah.
bridge: When the user has lost someone, especially a child or family member.
do_not_add: Do not add the age of the child or other details.

title: Umm Salamah's dua at her loss
summary: Umm Salamah learned from the Prophet ﷺ that whoever is struck by a loss and says 'To Allah we belong and to Him we return', asking Allah to reward them and replace it with something better, will be given something better. When her husband Abu Salamah died she said it, though she wondered who could be better than him. Later, the Prophet ﷺ himself proposed to her.
lesson: Say the dua even when you cannot imagine anything better. Allah's replacement can exceed what we picture.
bridge: When the user has lost a spouse or someone very close.
do_not_add: Do not present the remarriage as a promise to the user; the promise is 'something better', which Allah decides.

title: Hajar in the valley
summary: Ibrahim left Hajar and baby Isma'il in a barren valley. She asked him whether Allah had commanded this, and when he said yes, she said that then Allah would not abandon them. When the water ran out, she ran back and forth between the hills of Safa and Marwa searching, and Allah brought out the water of Zamzam.
lesson: Trust in Allah and effort go together: Hajar trusted, and still ran.
bridge: When the user feels alone, left behind, or is doing everything they can and still waiting.
do_not_add: Do not add the number of days or other details not in the hadith.

title: 'Do not grieve, Allah is with us'
summary: During the Hijrah, the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr hid in a cave while those hunting them came close. Abu Bakr feared they would be seen. The Prophet ﷺ reassured him: do not grieve, Allah is with us. Allah sent down tranquillity upon him.
lesson: Fear is human. The answer is remembering that Allah is with you.
bridge: When the user is afraid of something about to happen.
do_not_add: Do not add the spider web or birds' nest; these come from weak reports.

title: The angel of the mountains
summary: Aisha asked the Prophet ﷺ whether he had faced a day harder than Uhud. He described a day he called people to Allah and was rejected, and walked away overwhelmed with sorrow. Jibril came with the angel of the mountains, who offered to crush the people between two mountains. The Prophet ﷺ refused, hoping that their descendants would worship Allah alone.
lesson: When you are rejected or hurt, you can choose mercy and hope over revenge.
bridge: When the user has been rejected, humiliated or hurt by people.
do_not_add: Do not quote the well-known long Ta'if dua (its chain is weak). Do not add stoning details; they are not in this hadith.

title: Ka'b ibn Malik tells the truth
summary: Ka'b ibn Malik stayed behind from the expedition to Tabuk without an excuse. When the Prophet ﷺ returned, Ka'b chose to tell the truth instead of making excuses. He and two others were kept apart from the community for fifty nights, until the earth felt narrow to them. Then Allah revealed that He had accepted their repentance.
lesson: Honesty about a mistake is the start of repentance, and Allah accepts it.
bridge: When the user feels ashamed of a mistake and is tempted to hide or excuse it.
do_not_add: Keep the story short; do not add details beyond the hadith and 9:118.

title: The man who killed a hundred
summary: A man who had killed many people asked whether repentance was still possible for him. A scholar told him that nothing stands between a person and repentance, and to leave for a land where people worshipped Allah. He died on the way, and because he was nearer to that land, Allah forgave him.
lesson: No sin is too big for Allah's forgiveness when someone truly turns back.
bridge: When the user believes Allah could never forgive them.
do_not_add: Tell it gently and briefly. Do not dwell on the killings or add numbers beyond the hadith.

title: Adam and Hawwa turn back
summary: After eating from the tree, Adam and Hawwa did not blame each other or blame Allah. Together they said: our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will be among the losers. Allah accepted their repentance.
lesson: The first human mistake was followed by the first repentance. Turning back is part of being human.
bridge: When the user feels guilt and does not know how to begin repenting.
do_not_add: Do not blame Hawwa; the Qur'an addresses them both.

title: Yusuf forgives his brothers
summary: Years after his brothers threw him into a well, Yusuf stood before them as a man of authority, and they came to him in need. When they recognised him, he told them there was no blame on them that day, and asked Allah to forgive them.
lesson: Forgiving family can free you, even after deep hurt.
bridge: When the user is in conflict with family or holding an old hurt.
do_not_add: Do not name the wife of al-Aziz (the name 'Zulaikha' is not from the Qur'an or authentic hadith).

title: Abu Bakr keeps supporting Mistah
summary: Abu Bakr supported his poor relative Mistah, who later took part in spreading slander about Abu Bakr's daughter Aisha. Hurt, Abu Bakr swore to stop helping him. Allah revealed a verse asking people to pardon and overlook: do you not love that Allah should forgive you? Abu Bakr said that he did, and resumed his support.
lesson: Forgiving a relative who hurt you is a way of asking for Allah's forgiveness yourself.
bridge: When a relative has wronged the user and they are tempted to cut them off.
do_not_add: Do not retell the slander itself in detail.

title: The Bedouin who pulled his cloak
summary: A Bedouin pulled the Prophet's cloak so hard that it left a mark on his neck, and demanded to be given from Allah's wealth. The Prophet ﷺ turned to him, smiled, and ordered that he be given something.
lesson: Answering roughness with gentleness is the Prophet's way.
bridge: When someone has been rude or aggressive towards the user.
do_not_add: Do not add dialogue beyond the hadith.

title: 'Do not become angry'
summary: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ for advice. He said: do not become angry. The man asked again and again, and each time he gave the same answer. He also taught that the strong person is not the one who overpowers others, but the one who controls himself when angry.
lesson: Real strength is self-control in the moment of anger.
bridge: When the user is struggling with anger.
do_not_add: Keep to the meaning of the two hadith.

title: Sulayman and the ant
summary: As Sulayman's army approached, an ant warned the other ants to go into their homes. Sulayman heard it and smiled, and asked Allah to inspire him to be grateful for the blessings given to him and his parents, and to do good that pleases Him.
lesson: Even great blessings call us to gratitude, and small creatures can remind us.
bridge: When the user wants to be more grateful or is in a good moment.
do_not_add: Stay with the Qur'anic text.

title: 'Should I not be a grateful servant?'
summary: The Prophet ﷺ used to stand in night prayer until his feet cracked. Aisha asked why he did this when Allah had forgiven him. He replied: should I not love to be a grateful servant?
lesson: Gratitude is shown in actions, not only words.
bridge: When the user asks how to show gratitude to Allah.
do_not_add: Do not present this as an obligation for the user; it describes the Prophet's own devotion.

title: Khadijah's reassurance
summary: After the first revelation, the Prophet ﷺ came home trembling and told Khadijah he feared for himself. She comforted him: Allah would never disgrace him, because he kept family ties, carried the burdens of the weak, helped those in need, honoured guests and stood by people in hardship. Then she took him to her cousin Waraqah.
lesson: A spouse can be a place of safety: listening, reminding of the good, and finding help together.
bridge: When the user talks about marriage, or needs reassurance from people close to them.
do_not_add: Do not add details beyond the hadith.

title: Maryam and the palm tree
summary: Maryam withdrew alone to a distant place. The pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree, and she wished she had been forgotten. She was told not to grieve: Allah had placed a stream below her, and if she shook the trunk of the palm tree, fresh dates would fall. She was told to eat, drink and be at peace.
lesson: Even at your weakest, Allah asks for a small effort and sends the provision.
bridge: When the user feels alone and overwhelmed by physical or emotional pain.
do_not_add: Stay with the Qur'anic account.

title: Ibrahim and the fire
summary: When his people threw Ibrahim into a fire, he said: Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs. Allah commanded the fire to be cool and safe for Ibrahim.
lesson: Saying 'HasbunAllahu wa ni'mal wakil' is the response of the prophets when afraid.
bridge: When the user faces something frightening that is out of their control.
do_not_add: Do not add the size of the fire, a catapult, or how long it burned.
related_dua: Library item for 'HasbunAllahu wa ni'mal wakil'

title: Musa at the sea
summary: When Pharaoh's army closed in and the sea lay ahead, Musa's people cried that they were about to be caught. Musa said: no, my Lord is with me, He will guide me. Allah told him to strike the sea with his staff, and it parted.
lesson: When there seems to be no way out, certainty in Allah comes before the way opens.
bridge: When the user feels cornered with no options.
do_not_add: Stay with the Qur'anic account.

title: Yusuf in prison and the storehouses
summary: Yusuf was imprisoned unjustly. In prison he kept helping others, interpreting their dreams and calling them to Allah. Years later the king freed him, and Yusuf asked to be put in charge of the storehouses, saying he was a knowledgeable guardian. Allah established him in the land.
lesson: Keep serving and using your skills, even in a hard place. Your time may come.
bridge: When the user is stuck in a job they dislike or waiting for an opportunity.
do_not_add: Do not add how many years he spent in prison.

title: Musa asks for ease before a great task
summary: When Allah sent Musa to speak to Pharaoh, Musa asked Allah to expand his chest, make his task easy, and loosen the knot in his tongue so people would understand him.
lesson: Before something big, it is prophetic to ask Allah for calm, ease and clear words.
bridge: Before an exam, interview, presentation or difficult conversation.
do_not_add: Stay with the Qur'anic text.

title: Musa's journey to seek knowledge
summary: Musa set out to meet a servant of Allah with special knowledge, saying he would not give up until he reached him, even if it took a very long time. When he found him, he asked humbly to follow him and learn.
lesson: Learning needs determination, humility and patience.
bridge: When the user is studying hard or feels discouraged by how much they have to learn.
do_not_add: Keep to the Qur'an; do not add names or details from other sources.

title: The woman who chose patience
summary: A woman who suffered from seizures asked the Prophet ﷺ to pray for her cure. He offered her a choice: be patient and have Paradise, or he would pray for her cure. She chose patience, and asked only that he pray she would not become uncovered during her seizures, and he did.
lesson: Patience with illness is precious to Allah, and it is also fine to ask for practical help.
bridge: When the user lives with a long-term illness.
do_not_add: Do not suggest the user should refuse treatment. Islam encourages seeking treatment.
